config.title: Contains Duplicate

intro.title: Contains Duplicate
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that checks if an array contains any duplicate numbers. You will learn to use a hash set data structure to efficiently track and compare elements as you iterate through the array. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, loops, and the Set object. This beginner-friendly exercise will help you understand how to optimize for time complexity while solving a common algorithmic lesson.
intro.usecase: The Contains Duplicate algorithm is essential for data validation in real-world applications. In user registration forms, it prevents duplicate email addresses or usernames from being added to databases. E-commerce platforms use it to detect duplicate items in shopping carts before checkout. Content management systems apply it to ensure unique tags or categories aren't duplicated. This pattern also helps maintain data integrity in analytics dashboards by identifying duplicate records before processing.

objectives: Initialize a data structure to track encountered elements
Apply a loop to iterate through an array of numbers
Manipulate the tracking structure to check for duplicate entries
Construct a function that returns a boolean based on duplicate detection
Integrate conditional logic to handle early duplicate discovery
Configure the function to accept different input arrays
Implement the complete algorithm to solve the Contains Duplicate lesson

content.body: Have you ever wondered if there are duplicate items in a list? Let's learn how to check for duplicates efficiently. We'll discover a clever way to remember what we've already seen.
content.title: Welcome

content.body:
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
1. Explain why checking every pair is inefficient for large arrays.
2. Implement a solution using a lookup structure to track seen values.
3. Determine when to check for duplicates versus when to add to your tracking structure.
content.title: What you'll learn
Try it
content.prompt: Does this array have any duplicate numbers?

content.title: Try a bigger array
content.prompt: Does this array have any duplicates?

content.title: One more
content.prompt: Find any duplicates in this array
content.successMessage: Great! You found that 3 appears twice by checking each element against others.

content.body: What you just did was brute force: you checked each element against all the others until you found a match. This works for small arrays but becomes very slow as arrays grow larger.
content.title: What you did

content.body: When the array has 10,000 numbers, checking every pair takes millions of comparisons. We need a better method that scales well. Can't figure it out? Click Show me on the next step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: The key insight is to remember what we've already seen. Instead of re-scanning the array, we can use a lookup structure (like an object or Map) to track values we've encountered. Think of it like a notebook where we write down what we've seen and check it in one step.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: A notebook where we write down what we've seen and check it in one step.

content.body: We'll walk through the array once. For each number, we check if it's already in our notebook. If it is, we found a duplicate! If not, we add it to the notebook and continue.
content.title: The approach
content.illustratedExample:
Walkthrough with [2, 7, 11, 15, 7]:
- Check 2 → not in notebook → add 2
- Check 7 → not in notebook → add 7
- Check 11 → not in notebook → add 11
- Check 15 → not in notebook → add 15
- Check 7 → already in notebook! Found duplicate.

content.body:
1. Create an empty object to act as our 'notebook' for seen values.
2. Loop through each number in the array.
3. For each number, check if it exists as a key in our notebook.
4. If it exists, return true (duplicate found).
5. If not, add the number as a key to our notebook.
6. If loop completes without finding duplicates, return false.
content.title: Steps

steps.title: Create the function skeleton
steps.instruction: Start by creating a function called containsDuplicate that takes one parameter: nums.
steps.expectedOutcome: Function declaration with correct name and parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the function skeleton.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost there. Make sure the function is named containsDuplicate and takes nums as parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. We need a function named containsDuplicate that accepts nums.

steps.title: Create the lookup structure
steps.instruction: Inside the function, create an empty object called seen to track numbers we've encountered.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Now we have our 'notebook' ready.
steps.feedbackPartial: Close. Make sure you're creating an empty object with {}.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need an empty object to store seen values. Try const seen = {};

steps.title: Loop through the array
steps.instruction: Add a for loop to iterate through each number in nums. Use let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++.
steps.hint: The loop should go through all elements: for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) { }
steps.expectedOutcome: For loop that iterates through nums array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! Now we can examine each number.
steps.feedbackPartial: Almost. Make sure your loop goes from 0 to nums.length.
steps.feedbackWrong: We need a loop to go through all numbers. Try: for (let i = 0; i < nums.length; i++) { }

steps.title: Check and add to lookup structure
steps.instruction: Inside the loop, check if the current number exists in seen. If it does, return true. If not, add it to seen.
steps.hint: Use if (seen[nums[i]] !== undefined) to check, and seen[nums[i]] = true to add.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've implemented the efficient solution.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress. Make sure you're both checking and adding to the seen object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's think through this: check if number exists in seen, return true if it does, otherwise add it.

content.body: Congratulations! You've learned how to efficiently check for duplicates using a lookup structure. Remember: store values as keys in your object, check before adding, and you'll avoid unnecessary re-scanning. This approach scales beautifully to large arrays.
content.title: Done
